title: Amazon Account Health: How to Avoid Suspensions
headline: Amazon Account Health: How to Avoid Suspensions
description: A plain-language guide to Amazon account health: the Account Health page, common causes of warnings and suspensions, a weekly checklist and what to do if you get a notice.
body_html:
Your Amazon seller account is the asset everything else sits on. If it is suspended, listings go offline and funds can be held while you sort it out. Most suspensions follow warning signs that sellers could have spotted earlier. This guide explains, in plain language, what account health is, the problems that most often cause trouble, and a simple routine to stay safe. It is general information, not a guarantee, because Amazon decides and its rules change.

What "account health" means

Seller Central has an Account Health page that shows how your account is performing against Amazon's policies. It brings together customer service metrics, policy compliance, shipping performance and any notices from Amazon. Open it often. The exact targets differ by marketplace and selling plan and Amazon updates them, so always read the current numbers on your own dashboard instead of relying on a figure you saw in a video or forum post.

Common causes of account problems

  • Poor order performance. Late shipments, cancellations by the seller and a high rate of negative feedback or claims can all push your account towards the limit.
  • Product authenticity and condition complaints. Customers reporting "not as described", used items sold as new, or items that look counterfeit can trigger a review.
  • Intellectual property complaints. A brand owner can report your listing for using their trade mark, image or product without permission. See our guide on Brand Registry and trade marks for how brands protect themselves, and why you should only sell what you have the right to sell.
  • Restricted or prohibited products. Some categories and products need approval, and some are not allowed at all. Check the category rules before you buy stock.
  • Review and feedback manipulation. Asking friends for reviews, paying for reviews or offering incentives for positive reviews is against Amazon's rules.
  • Related accounts and identity problems. Using details that do not match your documents, or sharing a login in a way Amazon does not allow, can cause verification issues.
  • Misleading listings. Wrong claims, hidden variations or content that does not match the product can lead to removal.

A simple weekly routine

  • Open Account Health and read every notice, even ones that look minor.
  • Check shipping and cancellation numbers and fix the cause if they are drifting.
  • Read recent customer messages and returns for patterns, such as one product with repeated complaints.
  • Review any listing that gets claims or "not as described" returns. Update the images or text, or pause the product.
  • Check your email and the Seller Central notifications for policy messages. Answer deadlines promptly.
  • Keep supplier invoices and proof of authenticity ready. Amazon may ask for them.

If you receive a warning or suspension

  1. Do not panic and do not create a second account. That can make things worse.
  2. Read the notice carefully and find the exact policy and the reason given.
  3. Prepare an appeal or plan of action that explains the root cause, what you have already corrected, and what you will do to prevent it. Keep it factual and specific.
  4. Attach supporting documents such as invoices, supplier details or corrected listings, when the notice asks for them.
  5. Respond within the deadline and keep copies of everything you send.

No one can promise that an appeal will succeed. A clear, honest and well-documented response gives you the best chance. If you want to see how we handle access safely when helping a seller, read our guide on giving access to a service provider.

Habits that protect your account

  • Buy from suppliers you can document and keep the paperwork.
  • Write honest titles, bullets and images, and keep them updated. Our listing optimisation guide shows how to do that without exaggerating.
  • Use only permitted ways to ask for feedback.
  • Give your team access through Seller Central user permissions rather than sharing your password.
  • Keep your business, bank and tax details up to date.
